rationale: B wins because it has the discipline A almost has: it refuses to fake urgency where the fact block gives no dates. A's "Decay: 4hr — anchored on an active regulatory posture" is too confident; B's "No dated regulator action was supplied, so I cannot justify 4hr" is the editor brain doing its job. B also lands the sharpest safety point: "licensed-provider review...addresses prescribing, not manufacturing," which is exactly where a drug-safety reporter will stab first.
gaps_in_A: "Decay: 4hr — anchored on an active regulatory posture" overstates timing; the update says the FDA flagged risks, not when or how recently.
"The FDA risk flag is in play now" decorates an undated fact into a live peg. That is how a pitch gets kneecapped in the first reply.
"A newly profitable Hims & Hers bets its margins" is a plausible markets frame, but "margins" are not in the update. Fine as a question, too loose as a headline claim.
gaps_in_B: "Next step: `newsjack-detector`" is clever but not the cleanest next move. Before monitoring for pegs, the founder needs fact-checking on FDA action, pricing, profitability, and supplier identity.
"Decay: week" on the regulatory angle is cautious, but still a guess without the FDA date. Better than A's 4hr theatrics, still not sourced.
"The hook is a publicly traded telehealth company choosing the compounded side" is solid, but B misses the lab-testing service as a possible clinical-control proof point inside the regulatory angle.
